title: Fee Proposal
notes: Like the add service template, this is a FILLED example (212 Architects / SUNY Maritime Heritage Hall Renovation, March 2023), not a blank. Tokenizing means replacing live client values, so `forbid_in_output` asserts none survive.

HYBRID on purpose. This template carries 52 named bookmarks from an older Word automation, which are the best inventory of what the fields ARE and disambiguate a value appearing in several places. But their spans are NOT always the whole value, so short/ambiguous fields go through bookmarks and truncated ones through value matching.

THE TEMPLATE TRUNCATES THE PROJECT NAME, differently in three places: the cover reads 'SUNY Maritime Heritage Hall Renovation', the letter subject stops at '...Heritage Hal' and the body header at '...Hall Reno'. That is a live defect visible on every proposal. All three map to {{PROJECT_NAME}}, so tokenizing repairs it. Longest-first ordering matters or the short variants match inside the long one.

Eight bookmarks are collapsed to zero length and cannot be written into: txtClientCityLetter, txtClientStateLetter, txtClientZipLetter, txtProjectZip, txtClientCity, txtClientState, txtClientZip. The example never filled them. They need re-creating in Word before those fields can be used.
CoverCity1-8 are the office list, static branding rather than per-project, so they are left alone.
FEES ARE NOT TOKENIZED in this pass. txtDDFee holds 'Design Manual$12,240.00' -- label and amount in one bookmark -- and the fee table depends on the unresolved rate-table conflict. Separate job.
The example uses two different contact emails (KARCH@ on the letter, KSchmitt@ in the body). Both map to {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}.
Three different dates in the example (cover 3/31, letter 3/21, body 3/16) all map to {{DATE}}.
notes_rates: The hourly-rate list after PROPOSAL PROVISIONS was six hard-coded two-column lines (2023 rates, and lines 2-6 even lacked the $ on the left column). Line 1 is kept as a FOUR-token prototype (role/rate, tab, role/rate) and the app clones one paragraph per pair from project.hourlyRates; lines 2-6 are deleted. The '3% yearly escalation' sentence is policy text and stays.
notes_honorific: The body header read 'Ms. Jane' with the period OUTSIDE the txtPOCTitle3 bookmark while the letter reads '{{CONTACT_HONORIFIC}} {{CONTACT_NAME}}' with no period. Normalised so the app supplies the honorific WITH its period (Ms.) or drops the token and its trailing space entirely. Must run last in auto: it matches tokens that only exist after the bookmark pass.

block_ranges._note: PROPOSAL PROVISIONS. The template shipped BOTH the Standard and Alternate text of every pair plus a YYY/MM/DD placeholder; the section is now assembled from the library's provisions block (prov-preamble first). Title/body pair: bold Heading2 title line + indented Heading2 body, which is how the run-in Title. bodies are split by the app. Range ends at the hard-coded hourly-rate list, which stays as-is for now.

Attachment A. The template carried an OLDER unnumbered T&C; the firm standard now lives in pms_proposal_clauses block 'terms' and the app renders it into these prototypes. Heading1 auto-numbers via its style, so heading text is the bare title. Second occurrence of the anchor: the first is in the proposal body.

insert_sections._note: The template had no ASSUMPTIONS section; the library and the PMS do. Heading cloned from PROPOSAL PROVISIONS (Heading1, unnumbered), prototypes cloned from the Excluded pair (numbered Heading1 + ListParagraph) so assumptions list like exclusions. Sits between EXCLUDED SERVICES and PROPOSAL PROVISIONS, matching the app's box order.
